annotations.annotation: The pie chart represents the distribution of various categories related to scientific data. It consists of 26 slices, each labeled to indicate a different category. The largest slice is labeled "Chemical" in blue, which occupies 32% of the chart. "Protein" is in orange at 15%, while "DNA" in green covers around 6%. Several categories such as "Chemical Family," "Disease," and others like "Cell Type," "Drug," and "Frequency" are each approximately 5%. Smaller sections include labels like "Animal" in light blue, "Gene" in purple, "Organism Taxon" in brown, and others decreasing down to 1% or less. Some minor categories such as "Composite Mention," "Etymology," and "Disease Class," among others, feature very slender slices. The chart does not include a legend but offers percentage labels inside the slices, and it appears to order the segments in descending size starting from the largest. No slices are visually emphasized through techniques like exploding or offsetting.
